The Isthmus & Capitol Square 29

downtown, King St, Monona Terrace

  1. Must see · Markets & Cheese Shops · The Isthmus & Capitol Square

    Dane County Farmers' Market

    America's largest producers-only farmers' market (founded 1972): on summer Saturdays some 150 Wisconsin growers and cheesemakers completely encircle the State Capitol, and everything is grown or made by the person behind the stand. Time Out ranks it among the country's best. Order: Saturday-morning cheese curds, cheese bread and in-season produce sold by the people who made them.

    Capitol Square (Saturdays Apr–Nov), Madison, WI 53703

    Recommended by Wikipedia (notability + published coordinates), Destination Madison (CVB), Travel Wisconsin (WI Dept. of Tourism), Time Out — Madison

  2. Must see · Cheese Curds & Cheese · The Isthmus & Capitol Square

    Fromagination

    A European-style cut-to-order cheese shop on the Capitol Square since 2007, showcasing award-winning Wisconsin artisan cheesemakers — the obvious place to taste the state's cheese beyond curds. Order: Cut-to-order Wisconsin artisan cheese.

    12 S Carroll St, Madison, WI 53703

    Recommended by Isthmus, Time Out — Madison, Destination Madison (CVB), Brava Magazine

  3. Must see · The Isthmus & Capitol Square

    Wisconsin State Capitol

    The 1917 Beaux-Arts capitol at the heart of the Isthmus — the only granite capitol dome in the US. Free tours cover the rotunda mural 'The Resources of Wisconsin', and the summer observation deck gives a 360° view of the lakes. A National Historic Landmark (2001).

    Look for free tours; observation deck in summer

    2 E Main St, Madison, WI 53703

    Recommended by Wikipedia (notability + published coordinates), Visit The USA (Brand USA), Wisconsin Historical Society

  4. Must see · The Isthmus & Capitol Square

    Monona Terrace

    Frank Lloyd Wright's 1938 design for a civic center on Lake Monona, rejected by one vote and built only in 1997, nearly four decades after his death. The free rooftop garden is the city's best lake-and-Capitol view.

    1 John Nolen Dr, Madison, WI 53703

    Recommended by Wikipedia (notability + published coordinates), Frank Lloyd Wright Foundation, Saharchipedia

  5. Must see · Taverns, Brats & Burgers · The Isthmus & Capitol Square

    The Old Fashioned

    The Capitol Square's all-Wisconsin tavern and supper-club homage — Wisconsin beers, brandy old fashioneds and curds. Voted Madison's best cheese curds in the 2025 reader survey and named by Isthmus associate editor Linda Falkenstein among her top fish fries. Order: Beer-battered cheese curds (house recipe batter) and the Friday fish fry.

    23 N Pinckney St, Madison, WI 53703

    Recommended by Upnorthnews, City Cast Madison, The Infatuation (Madison reviews)

  6. Must see · Farm-to-Table & Fine Dining · The Isthmus & Capitol Square

    L'Etoile

    Madison's founding farm-to-table restaurant (Odessa Piper, 1976) on the Capitol Square — two of its chefs, Piper (2001) and Tory Miller (2012), won the James Beard Award for Best Chef: Midwest. Time Out's Madison list calls it out for working with more than 200 local vendors. Order: The seasonal farm-to-table tasting menu, sourced from 200+ local vendors.

    1 S Pinckney St, Madison, WI 53703

    Recommended by James Beard Foundation, Time Out — Madison, Isthmus

  7. Must see · European (Swiss, German, Norwegian, Italian) · The Isthmus & Capitol Square

    Osteria Papavero

    An intimate Italian osteria (2006) off the Capitol Square; Bologna-raised chef Francesco Mangano advanced to James Beard Best Chef: Midwest nominee in 2023. Order: Chef Francesco Mangano's Bologna- and Tuscany-rooted Italian cooking.

    128 E Wilson St, Madison, WI 53703

    Recommended by James Beard Foundation, Madison Magazine / Channel 3000, The Cap Times

  8. Must see · European (Swiss, German, Norwegian, Italian) · The Isthmus & Capitol Square

    Cento

    Capitol Square Italian in a brick-and-stained-glass historic office building; Best of Madison 2026 silver for Restaurant, bronze for Italian and Chef (Edwin Ramirez); reviewed by Isthmus, The Takeout and the Daily Cardinal. Order: Handmade pasta (gnocchi with mushrooms and breadcrumbs) and wood-fired pizza.

    122 W Mifflin St, Madison, WI 53703

    Recommended by Madison Magazine / Channel 3000, Isthmus, The Takeout

  9. Must see · The Isthmus & Capitol Square

    Madison Museum of Contemporary Art (MMoCA)

    Free contemporary-art museum in the Cesar Pelli–designed Overture complex at the top of State Street, with a rooftop sculpture garden.

    State St (Overture Center complex), Madison, WI 53703

    Recommended by Destination Madison (CVB), Wikipedia (notability + published coordinates)

  10. Must see · Breweries, Wineries & Distilleries · The Isthmus & Capitol Square

    The Robin Room

    Chad Vogel's 2016 lounge that 'catapulted Madison's cocktail scene' (Imbibe); on City Cast's must-try cocktails and coziest-spots lists. Order: The Jasmine (gin, Campari, Cointreau, lemon) or a seasonal house cocktail.

    821 E Johnson St, Madison, WI 53703

    Recommended by Imbibe Magazine — Where to Drink in Madison, City Cast Madison

  11. Worth the detour · Taverns, Brats & Burgers · The Isthmus & Capitol Square

    The Plaza Tavern

    A Prohibition-era (1930) downtown tavern that invented the double-stack Plazaburger and still won't reveal its sauce; on City Cast's oldest-restaurants and best-dive-bars lists, a Daily Cardinal 'bite of the week'. Order: The Plazaburger with the secret sauce (since 1963–64).

    319 N Henry St, Madison, WI 53703

    Recommended by City Cast Madison, Travel Wisconsin (WI Dept. of Tourism), Madison Magazine / Channel 3000, The Daily Cardinal (UW–Madison)

  12. Worth the detour · Breweries, Wineries & Distilleries · The Isthmus & Capitol Square

    Great Dane Pub & Brewing Co.

    Madison's flagship brewpub since November 1994, in the NRHP-listed Fess Hotel (1858) at Doty & King; UpNorthNews readers' #1 Madison brewery 2025. Order: House-brewed Good Dog IPA or Black Earth Porter in the 1858 Fess Hotel.

    123 E Doty St, Madison, WI 53703

    Recommended by Upnorthnews, Isthmus, Madison Magazine / Channel 3000, Wikipedia (notability + published coordinates)

  13. Worth the detour · The Isthmus & Capitol Square

    Orpheum Theater

    A 1927 Rapp & Rapp movie palace a block from the Capitol — Art Deco outside, French Renaissance within — still a live-music hall; on the National Register.

    216 State St, Madison, WI 53703

    Recommended by Wikipedia (notability + published coordinates), Isthmus, Wisconsin Historical Society

  14. Worth the detour · The Isthmus & Capitol Square

    Wisconsin Veterans Museum

    Free state museum on Capitol Square tracing Wisconsin's military history from the Civil War (including Old Abe, the war eagle) to the present. The state has bought the building to replace it with a new five-story museum — check before visiting as construction nears.

    30 W Mifflin St, Madison, WI 53703

    Recommended by Destination Madison (CVB), Wikipedia (notability + published coordinates), Wisconsin Public Radio

  15. Worth the detour · The Isthmus & Capitol Square

    Gates of Heaven Synagogue

    Wisconsin's first synagogue (1863, August Kutzbock) — among the oldest surviving in the U.S.; moved to James Madison Park in 1971 to escape demolition.

    302 E Gorham St (James Madison Park), Madison, WI 53703

    Recommended by Wikipedia (notability + published coordinates), Madison365, Wisconsin Historical Society

  16. Worth the detour · The Isthmus & Capitol Square

    Tenney Park & the Tenney Lock

    O.C. Simonds' 1899 park — 'Madison's prettiest place to skate' on the lagoon (Isthmus) — and the Yahara's busiest boat lock; NRHP-listed city landmark.

    1414 E Johnson St, Madison, WI 53703

    Recommended by Isthmus, City of Madison Parks, Dane County Parks (official)

  17. Worth the detour · Supper Clubs & Brandy Old Fashioneds · The Isthmus & Capitol Square

    Tornado Club Steak House

    Off the Capitol Square, an old-school supper-club steakhouse with classic service — 2012 James Beard Best Chef Tory Miller's date-night pick, and runner-up for Madison's best old fashioned in the 2025 reader vote. Order: Barrel-aged brandy old fashioned and old-school steakhouse steaks.

    116 S Hamilton St, Madison, WI 53703

    Recommended by JBF Editorial, Upnorthnews, Time Out — Madison

  18. Worth the detour · Pizza · The Isthmus & Capitol Square

    Ian's Pizza

    The late-night State Street slice shop that made mac-and-cheese pizza a Madison rite of passage. On Time Out's Madison restaurant list and its best-things-to-do roundup. Order: Mac n' cheese pizza by the slice, served until 2:30am.

    100 State St, Madison, WI 53703

    Recommended by Time Out — Madison, Isthmus, Travel Wisconsin (WI Dept. of Tourism)

  19. Worth the detour · European (Swiss, German, Norwegian, Italian) · The Isthmus & Capitol Square

    Essen Haus

    A Bavarian 'trinken halle' on East Wilson with 16 German taps, the passed-around glass boot, lederhosen-clad servers and live polka every Friday and Saturday — Madison's German-immigrant roots, played loud. Order: Two-liter glass beer boots of German tap beer, soft pretzels with mustard; weekend oompah.

    514 E Wilson St, Madison, WI 53703

    Recommended by Isthmus, Travel Wisconsin (WI Dept. of Tourism), The Badger Herald

  20. Worth the detour · Taverns, Brats & Burgers · The Isthmus & Capitol Square

    Tipsy Cow

    Burger-and-whisky bar at the point of King and Main off the Square; bronze for Cheese Curds and Burger and a Best Bar medal in Best of Madison 2025; on UpNorthNews' best-curds list. Order: Beer-battered curds with Tipsy sauce; Wisconsin butter burger.

    King St at Main St, Capitol Square, Madison, WI 53703

    Recommended by Madison Magazine / Channel 3000, Upnorthnews, Isthmus

  21. Worth the detour · The Isthmus & Capitol Square

    Overture Center for the Arts

    César Pelli's 2004 performing-arts center at the top of State Street — Overture Hall, the restored Capitol Theater and, next door, the Madison Museum of Contemporary Art.

    201 State St, Madison, WI 53703

    Recommended by Wikipedia (notability + published coordinates), Saharchipedia

  22. Worth the detour · The Isthmus & Capitol Square

    Madison Children's Museum

    A hands-on museum off the Capitol Square, rebuilt green with the year-round 'Rooftop Ramble' garden (chickens included) — named one of the top five US children's museums by Parents magazine.

    100 N Hamilton St, Madison, WI 53703

    Recommended by Wikipedia (notability + published coordinates), Architect magazine (aia)

  23. Worth the detour · American & New American · The Isthmus & Capitol Square

    Graze

    Tory Miller's more casual, glass-walled sibling to L'Etoile on the Square (opened 2010), still farm-sourced; Madison Magazine marked its 15th year. Order: Seasonal farm-to-table gastropub plates with a view of the Capitol.

    1 S Pinckney St, Madison, WI 53703

    Recommended by Isthmus, Madison Magazine / Channel 3000

  24. Worth the detour · Pizza · The Isthmus & Capitol Square

    Lucille

    A tri-level King Street pizzeria and cocktail bar in the old Isthmus building (2016), with a weekly jazz night; in Travel Wisconsin's first-timer's guide to eating in Madison. Order: Wood-fired pizza and craft cocktails; Wednesday-night live jazz.

    101 King St, Madison, WI 53703

    Recommended by Travel Wisconsin (WI Dept. of Tourism), The Cap Times

  25. Worth the detour · Breakfast, Cafés & Coffee · The Isthmus & Capitol Square

    Marigold Kitchen

    Downtown brunch standby — gold for Breakfast/Brunch in Best of Madison 2026 (silver 2025), and on UpNorthNews' best-brunch roundup. Order: Locally sourced weekend brunch plates.

    Downtown (Capitol Square area), Madison, WI

    Recommended by Madison Magazine / Channel 3000, Upnorthnews

  26. Worth the detour · Farm-to-Table & Fine Dining · The Isthmus & Capitol Square

    Heritage Tavern

    Farm-to-table tavern with a James Beard–semifinalist chef, on City Cast's cocktail roundup and UpNorthNews' best-brunch list. Order: Farm-to-table plates and reimagined brunch staples; weekday happy-hour cocktails.

    Downtown Madison, WI

    Recommended by City Cast Madison, Upnorthnews

  27. Deep cut · The Isthmus & Capitol Square

    Robert M. Lamp House

    Madison's oldest Wright-designed house (1903), built for his boyhood friend 'Robie' Lamp and hidden inside a downtown block two streets from the Capitol — Atlas Obscura calls it an Easter egg. Exterior only.

    Look for private — exterior only

    22 N Butler St, Madison, WI 53703

    Recommended by Atlas Obscura, Wikipedia (notability + published coordinates), Wisconsin Historical Society

  28. Deep cut · European (Swiss, German, Norwegian, Italian) · The Isthmus & Capitol Square

    The Coopers Tavern

    Irish-born Peter McElvanna's Capitol Square gastropub (2010) uniting 'Irish and Midwestern flavors' (Isthmus); Destination Madison-listed. Order: The Reuben in the snug, with an Irish whiskey.

    20 W Mifflin St, Madison, WI 53703

    Recommended by Isthmus, Destination Madison (CVB), Travel Wisconsin (WI Dept. of Tourism)

  29. Closed — kept for the record · Breakfast, Cafés & Coffee · The Isthmus & Capitol Square

    Short Stack Eatery — CLOSED

    A downtown all-day breakfast spot on Time Out's Madison list for more than a decade — it announced its permanent closure in January 2025 (WMTV). Kept on the map flagged closed. Order: Pancake-forward breakfast and brunch.

    301 W Johnson St, Madison, WI 53703

    Recommended by Time Out — Madison, Travel Wisconsin (WI Dept. of Tourism), WMTV 15 News

UW–Madison campus & State Street 22

Bascom Hill, Memorial Union, Picnic Point

  1. Must see · UW–Madison campus & State Street

    Memorial Union Terrace

    The lakeside terrace of the 1928 Memorial Union on Lake Mendota — the city's 'unofficial living room', with sunburst chairs in John Deere green, Allis-Chalmers orange and yellow, a beer and a Babcock cone at sunset. The Union is on the National Register.

    800 Langdon St, Madison, WI 53706

    Recommended by Visit The USA (Brand USA), Wikipedia (notability + published coordinates), Wisconsin Historical Society

  2. Must see · UW–Madison campus & State Street

    Chazen Museum of Art

    UW–Madison's free art museum — 25,000 works across two buildings, the second a 2011 Machado-Silvetti addition — the second-largest collection in Wisconsin.

    Look for free admission

    750 University Ave, Madison, WI 53706

    Recommended by Wikipedia (notability + published coordinates), Travel Wisconsin (WI Dept. of Tourism), Destination Madison (CVB)

  3. Must see · UW–Madison campus & State Street

    Picnic Point

    A wooded peninsula that juts nearly a mile into Lake Mendota inside UW's 300-acre Lakeshore Nature Preserve — a flat walk to fire circles at the tip with the Capitol skyline across the water. On the north shore, Atlas Obscura's never-opened 1968 'Wright-style' beach house.

    Look for free

    Lakeshore Nature Preserve, Univ. Bay Dr entrance, Madison, WI 53705

    Recommended by Destination Madison (CVB), Travel Wisconsin (WI Dept. of Tourism), Atlas Obscura

  4. Must see · Breweries, Wineries & Distilleries · UW–Madison campus & State Street

    Der Rathskeller

    The Memorial Union's 1928 German-style beer hall: when its first keg was tapped in 1933, UW became the first public university in the US to serve beer. Eugene Hausler's murals and riddles, restored after the union's renovation, and the 'Battle of Beer and Wine' next door in der Stiftskeller. Order: A Wisconsin tap beer under the 1928 Hausler murals and 300 steins (then out to the Terrace).

    Memorial Union, 800 Langdon St, Madison, WI 53706

    Recommended by Destination Madison (CVB), Isthmus, UW–Madison News

  5. Must see · Ice Cream & Frozen Custard · UW–Madison campus & State Street

    Babcock Hall Dairy Store

    The UW dairy plant's own shop since 1951 — the nation's oldest university dairy facility, making ~75,000 gallons in 90+ flavors from Wisconsin milk. Silver for Ice Cream in Best of Madison 2025. Order: Union Utopia (or Mnookie Dough) scooped from the campus dairy plant.

    1605 Linden Dr, Madison, WI 53706

    Recommended by Travel Wisconsin (WI Dept. of Tourism), Madison Magazine / Channel 3000, The Daily Cardinal (UW–Madison)

  6. Must see · Taverns, Brats & Burgers · UW–Madison campus & State Street

    The Nitty Gritty

    Opened 1968 as a blues club, 'Madison's Official Birthday Bar' since 1985 (330,000 birthdays); rebuilt after a 2023 fire; silver for Burger in Best of Madison 2025. Doug Moe on its storied history (Madison Magazine). Order: The Grittyburger with Gritty Sauce — and a free birthday beer in a commemorative mug.

    223 N Frances St, Madison, WI 53703

    Recommended by Madison Magazine / Channel 3000, The Daily Cardinal (UW–Madison), Travel Wisconsin (WI Dept. of Tourism)

  7. Must see · UW–Madison campus & State Street

    Bascom Hill & the Lincoln statue

    The steep historic quad at the heart of campus, crowned by Bascom Hall and Adolph Weinman's seated Abraham Lincoln — the most-photographed spot for graduating seniors, who climb into his lap. Free.

    Bascom Hill, UW–Madison campus, Madison, WI 53706

    Recommended by Destination Madison (CVB), Wikipedia (notability + published coordinates)

  8. Must see · European (Swiss, German, Norwegian, Italian) · UW–Madison campus & State Street

    Paul's Pel'meni

    Late-night student institution serving a single dish of Russian dumplings; on The Infatuation's 14 best restaurants in Madison and a Daily Cardinal favorite. Order: Pel'meni (beef or potato) with butter, sour cream, curry and cilantro — the whole menu.

    State St area, Madison, WI

    Recommended by The Infatuation (Madison reviews), The Daily Cardinal (UW–Madison)

  9. Worth the detour · UW–Madison campus & State Street

    Camp Randall Stadium

    The Badgers' 1917 stadium on a Civil War training-camp site — come for a home game and 'Jump Around' between the third and fourth quarters, when 76,000 people make the stands sway.

    1440 Monroe St, Madison, WI 53711

    Recommended by Wikipedia (notability + published coordinates), The Daily Cardinal (UW–Madison), WTMJ (Milwaukee)

  10. Worth the detour · UW–Madison campus & State Street

    Science Hall

    An 1888 red-brick Romanesque pile at the foot of Bascom Hill (and a fixture of Accidentally Wes Anderson), where Charles Van Hise built geology's national reputation — a National Historic Landmark since 1993.

    550 N Park St, Madison, WI 53706

    Recommended by NPS, Wikipedia (notability + published coordinates), Wisconsin Historical Society

  11. Worth the detour · Taverns, Brats & Burgers · UW–Madison campus & State Street

    Dotty Dumpling's Dowry

    A longstanding campus-edge burger institution off State Street, its ceiling hung with kites and memorabilia. On Time Out's Madison list; Isthmus calls burgers 'the heart and soul of Dotty's'. Order: Thick hand-made burgers cooked to order, with 14 cheeses to choose from.

    317 N Frances St, Madison, WI 53703

    Recommended by Time Out — Madison, Isthmus, Travel Wisconsin (WI Dept. of Tourism)

  12. Worth the detour · European (Swiss, German, Norwegian, Italian) · UW–Madison campus & State Street

    Teddywedgers

    Pasty counter at the top of State Street since 1976, carrying on the Cornish-miner pasty of SW Wisconsin's lead region; Madison Magazine calls it a Madison staple, and it anchors State Trunk Tour's Wisconsin pasty-shop guide. Order: Traditional Cornish pasty (steak, potato, onion) — the Mineral Point miners' lunch.

    101 State St, Madison, WI 53703

    Recommended by Madison Magazine / Channel 3000, State Trunk Tour, The Badger Herald

  13. Worth the detour · UW–Madison campus & State Street

    Allen Centennial Garden

    A free 2.5-acre teaching garden around the 1896 Victorian dean's house on the ag campus — themed rooms from a Dutch to a New American garden, featured in The American Gardener.

    Look for free

    10 Babcock Dr, Madison, WI 53706

    Recommended by Wikipedia (notability + published coordinates), Wisconsin Alumni Association

  14. Worth the detour · UW–Madison campus & State Street

    Observatory Hill Mound Group

    A bird effigy and a rare two-tailed water-spirit mound just west of Washburn Observatory, overlooking Lake Mendota (NRHP). Free.

    Observatory Hill, UW–Madison campus, Madison, WI

    Recommended by OnMilwaukee, Wikipedia (notability + published coordinates)

  15. Worth the detour · UW–Madison campus & State Street

    UW–Madison Geology Museum

    Free campus museum in Weeks Hall: Wisconsin's deep past in rocks, fossils, meteorites, a fluorescent-mineral room, dinosaurs and a mastodon skeleton.

    Weeks Hall, UW–Madison campus, Madison, WI

    Recommended by Destination Madison (CVB), Wikipedia (notability + published coordinates)

  16. Worth the detour · UW–Madison campus & State Street

    L. R. Ingersoll Physics Museum

    A 1918 hands-on physics museum — one of the first of its kind — with 65+ interactive exhibits built by faculty and students; free on weekdays.

    Chamberlin Hall, UW–Madison campus, Madison, WI

    Recommended by Atlas Obscura, Wikipedia (notability + published coordinates)

  17. Worth the detour · UW–Madison campus & State Street

    Lakeshore Nature Preserve & Lakeshore Path

    300 acres along four miles of Lake Mendota's south shore; the Lakeshore Path runs from the Memorial Union through woods and prairie out to Picnic Point. Free.

    South shore of Lake Mendota, UW–Madison campus, Madison, WI

    Recommended by Destination Madison (CVB), Wikipedia (notability + published coordinates)

  18. Worth the detour · UW–Madison campus & State Street

    The Red Gym (UW Armory and Gymnasium)

    1894 castle-like armory-gymnasium on Lake Mendota's shore — a National Historic Landmark (1993) that now houses UW's visitor and welcome center.

    716 Langdon St, Madison, WI 53706

    Recommended by NPS, Wikipedia (notability + published coordinates)

  19. Worth the detour · UW–Madison campus & State Street

    North Hall (University of Wisconsin)

    The university's first building (1851), on Bascom Hill — John Muir's dorm 1860–63; a National Historic Landmark since 1965.

    Bascom Hill, UW–Madison campus, Madison, WI 53706

    Recommended by NPS, Wikipedia (notability + published coordinates)

  20. Worth the detour · UW–Madison campus & State Street

    Union South & the Sett

    The 2011 Prairie-style union steps from Camp Randall — bowling, billiards and a two-story climbing wall at the Sett; Badger Bash with the UW Marching Band before every home game.

    1308 W Dayton St, Madison, WI 53715

    Recommended by UW–Madison News, WMTV 15 News

  21. Deep cut · Taverns, Brats & Burgers · UW–Madison campus & State Street

    Jordan's Big 10 Pub

    The Camp Randall pre-game fixture with Regent Street's largest outdoor beer garden — City Cast Madison's tailgate pick; OnMilwaukee's Madison sports-bar guide; Madison Magazine's Regent St game-day story. Order: A game-day beer in Regent Street's biggest beer garden.

    1330 Regent St, Madison, WI 53715

    Recommended by City Cast Madison, OnMilwaukee, Madison Magazine / Channel 3000

  22. Deep cut · UW–Madison campus & State Street

    Washburn Observatory

    UW's 1881 observatory on Observatory Hill above Lake Mendota; its 15.6-inch Clark refractor still opens to the public on clear-night open houses.

    1401 Observatory Dr, Madison, WI 53706

    Recommended by Wikipedia (notability + published coordinates), UW–Madison Libraries

East side 25

Willy Street, Atwood, Schenk-Atwood, Monona & the north side

  1. Must see · Hmong, Lao & Southeast Asian · East side

    Ahan

    'Ahan' means food in Lao: Jamie and Chuckie Brown-Soukaseume's Willy Street restaurant cooks from Jamie's Lao childhood with Wisconsin ingredients. James Beard semifinalist for Best Chef: Midwest (2025) after an Emerging Chef nod; reviewed by Isthmus and profiled by PBS Wisconsin. Order: Beef laab (Lao beef salad with toasted rice powder) and Luang Prabang-style khao soi in clear chicken broth.

    744 Williamson St, Madison, WI 53703

    Recommended by James Beard Foundation, The Cap Times, Isthmus, PBS Wisconsin, Travel Wisconsin (WI Dept. of Tourism)

  2. Must see · Supper Clubs & Brandy Old Fashioneds · East side

    Toby's Supper Club

    A south-east-side roadhouse supper club in some form since the 1930s, still family-run, with the relish tray, cinnamon rolls and frog legs of the classic Wisconsin menu. Swept the 2025 Madison reader vote: best restaurant, best fish fry and best old fashioned. Order: Friday cod or catfish fish fry, fried perch, the hand-mixed brandy old fashioned, hashbrowns with American cheese on top.

    3717 S Dutch Mill Rd, Madison, WI 53718

    Recommended by Upnorthnews, The Cap Times, Isthmus, Travel Wisconsin (WI Dept. of Tourism)

  3. Must see · Hmong, Lao & Southeast Asian · East side

    Lao Laan-Xang

    Madison's first Laotian restaurant, family-run since 1989; the original Willy Street room closed in 2022 but the Atwood Avenue location carries on. On Time Out's Madison list and profiled by Brava and Experience Wisconsin. Order: Laotian classics — moak pa (fish steamed in banana leaf), curry squash, larb and the eggrolls.

    2098 Atwood Ave, Madison, WI 53704

    Recommended by Time Out — Madison, Brava Magazine, Experience Wisconsin magazine, Madison365

  4. Must see · Farm-to-Table & Fine Dining · East side

    Sardine

    French bistro in a converted warehouse on the Lake Monona shore; on The Infatuation's 14 best in Madison, Imbibe's where-to-drink list (best bar seat for a Martini and oysters) and runner-up best restaurant + best view in UpNorthNews readers' 2025 vote. Order: Moules-frites, steak frites with shallot butter, and the gruyère-draped bar hot dog.

    617 Williamson St, Madison, WI 53703

    Recommended by The Infatuation (Madison reviews), Imbibe Magazine — Where to Drink in Madison, Upnorthnews, Travel Wisconsin (WI Dept. of Tourism)

  5. Must see · Bakeries & Kringle · East side

    Madison Sourdough

    A European-style bakery-café that mills around 40% of its own flour from local farmers' grain; baker Andrew Hutchison was a 2023 James Beard semifinalist (Outstanding Bakery/pastry) and Travel Wisconsin calls it 'a Madison must for breakfast'. Order: Naturally leavened breads from flour milled in-house, croissants (almond, cheddar-chive) and the cinnamon roll.

    916 Williamson St, Madison, WI 53703

    Recommended by James Beard Foundation, Travel Wisconsin (WI Dept. of Tourism), Madison Magazine / Channel 3000

  6. Must see · Bakeries & Kringle · East side

    Gail Ambrosius Chocolatier

    Atwood Avenue chocolatier working in single-origin dark chocolate (an Isthmus cover story); gold for Chocolate in Best of Madison 2026; on Brava's and Experience Wisconsin's chocolate-shop lists. Order: Single-origin dark-chocolate truffles with spices and teas.

    2083 Atwood Ave, Madison, WI 53704

    Recommended by Madison Magazine / Channel 3000, Isthmus, Brava Magazine

  7. Must see · East side

    Olbrich Botanical Gardens & Thai Pavilion

    16 acres of free outdoor gardens on Lake Monona plus the Bolz Conservatory glass pyramid — and the gilded Royal Thai Pavilion, a gift of the Thai government and the only one on the US mainland.

    Look for outdoor gardens free

    3330 Atwood Ave, Madison, WI 53704

    Recommended by Visit The USA (Brand USA), Atlas Obscura

  8. Must see · Farm-to-Table & Fine Dining · East side

    Mint Mark

    Produce-forward small plates from an open kitchen on East Washington, built on Wisconsin farms and local spirits. Its chefs have been James Beard semifinalists in two separate years — Sean Pharr (2024) and Kasey Lee Cooke (2026) — and Travel Wisconsin puts it in its first-timer's guide to eating in Madison. Order: Wisconsin-farm small plates that rotate weekly, and a Friday-night fish fry.

    1874 E Washington Ave, Madison, WI 53704

    Recommended by James Beard Foundation, Travel Wisconsin (WI Dept. of Tourism)

  9. Worth the detour · Taverns, Brats & Burgers · East side

    The Weary Traveler Freehouse

    A dim, deep-booth Willy Street pub since 2002, walls lined with travel posters; its award-winning burger is the order. On Time Out's Madison list and in the 2025 reader vote for best bar food. Order: Bob's Bad Breath Burger — half a pound with cream cheese, green goddess, caramelized onions and garlic.

    1201 Williamson St, Madison, WI 53703

    Recommended by Time Out — Madison, Isthmus, Madison Magazine / Channel 3000, Upnorthnews

  10. Worth the detour · Taverns, Brats & Burgers · East side

    Dexter's Pub

Order: A house-made liqueur/aperitif cocktail (e.g. the pineapple-sage).

    1401 Northern Ct, Madison, WI 53703

    Recommended by James Beard Foundation, Isthmus, The Cap Times, Madison Magazine / Channel 3000

  12. Worth the detour · East side

    1353 Williamson St, Madison, WI 53703

    Recommended by Madison Magazine / Channel 3000, Travel Wisconsin (WI Dept. of Tourism), Isthmus

  19. Worth the detour · Breweries, Wineries & Distilleries · East side

    Recommended by Upnorthnews, Madison Magazine / Channel 3000

    2105 Sherman Ave, Madison, WI 53704

    Recommended by Madison Magazine / Channel 3000, Isthmus

    99 Cambridge Rd, Maple Bluff, WI 53704

    Recommended by Wikipedia (notability + published coordinates), Wisconsin Historical Society, Wisconsin Dept. of Administration

    2089 Atwood Ave, Madison, WI 53704

    Recommended by Time Out — Madison, Wisconsin State Journal (madison.com), Isthmus

  23. Deep cut · East side

    Two animal effigies — a lynx and a bear — plus a linear mound on the Lake Monona side of the east isthmus (NRHP). Free.

    Elmside Park, Madison, WI

    Recommended by OnMilwaukee, Wikipedia (notability + published coordinates)

  24. Deep cut · Mexican & Latin · East side

    6005 Monona Dr, Monona, WI 53716

    Recommended by Time Out — Madison, Isthmus

  25. Deep cut · Taverns, Brats & Burgers · East side

    Player's Sports Bar & Grill

    Atwood neighborhood sports bar City Cast credits with Madison's best bar burgers; silver Sports Bar in Best of Madison 2026. Order: The bar burger City Cast calls the best in town.

    Atwood neighborhood, Madison, WI

    Recommended by City Cast Madison, Madison Magazine / Channel 3000

West side 25

Monroe Street, the Arboretum, Hilldale & Odana

  1. Must see · Breakfast, Cafés & Coffee · West side

    Mickies Dairy Bar

    A cash-only breakfast diner across from Camp Randall since 1947, with a reader-board menu and portions of legend. First on Time Out's Madison list; the Cap Times covered the founding family handing it to new owners rather than closing it. Order: The famously massive Scrambler, plate-sized pancakes and crispy hash browns (cash only).

    1511 Monroe St, Madison, WI 53711

    Recommended by Time Out — Madison, Isthmus, The Cap Times, Travel Wisconsin (WI Dept. of Tourism)

  2. Must see · West side

    UW–Madison Arboretum

    The world's first restored ecological communities — prairies, savannas and wetlands started by Aldo Leopold and CCC crews in the 1930s — now a National Historic Landmark (2021) with a free trail network. Atlas Obscura's 'Lost City Forest' is the failed 1920s subdivision inside it.

    Look for free

    1207 Seminole Hwy, Madison, WI 53711

    Recommended by NPS, Visit The USA (Brand USA), Atlas Obscura

  3. Must see · West side

    Jacobs House (Wright's first Usonian)

    Frank Lloyd Wright's 1937 house for journalist Herbert Jacobs — often cited as his first Usonian design, and one of eight Wright buildings inscribed together as a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2019. A private home: view from the street.

    Look for private residence — exterior only

    441 Toepfer Ave, Madison, WI 53711

    Recommended by UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Wikipedia (notability + published coordinates), WMTV 15 News

  4. Must see · West side

    First Unitarian Society Meeting House

    Wright's own congregation's church (1949–51), its copper-clad prow roof rising like hands in prayer — a National Historic Landmark (2004) with public tours.

    900 University Bay Dr, Shorewood Hills, WI 53705

    Recommended by NPS, Wikipedia (notability + published coordinates), Wisconsin Historical Society

  5. Must see · Farm-to-Table & Fine Dining · West side

    Fairchild

    A small Monroe Street dining room in a century-old brick building whose chef-owners Itaru Nagano and Andrew Kroeger won the 2023 James Beard Award for Best Chef: Midwest — the third Madison chef ever to take it. Order: A short, seasonal menu — snacks like deviled eggs, a seasonal soup, a couple of pastas and entrées such as halibut.

    2611 Monroe St, Madison, WI 53711

    Recommended by James Beard Foundation, The Cap Times

  6. Must see · European (Swiss, German, Norwegian, Italian) · West side

    Lombardino's

    On University Avenue since 1952 (City Cast's oldest-restaurants list); Best of Madison 2026 gold for Italian, silver for Chef (Andres Martinez) and bronze for Upscale Dining. Order: Classic red-sauce Italian-American — housemade pasta and a martini at the bar.

    University Ave, Madison, WI

    Recommended by Madison Magazine / Channel 3000, City Cast Madison

  7. Worth the detour · West side

    Henry Vilas Zoo

    A 28-acre AZA-accredited county zoo beside Lake Wingra that has been free since 1904 — a condition of the Vilas family's land gift.

    Look for free admission

    Henry Vilas Park, Madison, WI

    Recommended by Wikipedia (notability + published coordinates), Travel Wisconsin (WI Dept. of Tourism), Saharchipedia

  8. Worth the detour · West side

    Forest Hill Cemetery

    Madison's 1857 garden cemetery: seven effigy mounds from 700–1200 CE (a goose flying toward Lake Wingra, two panthers), Confederate Rest for prisoners who died at Camp Randall, and governors and senators. The city publishes a walking tour.

    Look for free

    1 Speedway Rd, Madison, WI 53705

    Recommended by Wikipedia (notability + published coordinates), City of Madison Parks, The Clio

  9. Worth the detour · West side

    Frank W. Hoyt Park

    Drumlin-top park with Depression-era CWA/WPA rustic stone shelter, fireplaces, stairs and the Sunset Point lookout, plus 1850s sandstone quarries; on the National Register since 2018.

    3902 Regent St, Madison, WI 53705

    Recommended by Wikipedia (notability + published coordinates), Wisconsin Historical Society, Saharchipedia

  10. Worth the detour · Farm-to-Table & Fine Dining · West side

    2433 University Ave, Madison, WI 53726

    Recommended by James Beard Foundation, The Cap Times, Wisconsin Public Radio

  11. Worth the detour · Mediterranean, Middle Eastern & African · West side

    6119 Odana Rd, Madison, WI 53719

    Recommended by Isthmus, Madison Magazine / Channel 3000, The Cap Times

  12. Worth the detour · European (Swiss, German, Norwegian, Italian) · West side

Order: Handmade pasta with Amalfi-coast seafood; brick-oven pizza; limoncello cocktails.

    2903 University Ave, Madison, WI 53705

    Recommended by The Cap Times, Madison Magazine / Channel 3000, City Cast Madison

  13. Worth the detour · Taverns, Brats & Burgers · West side

    West-side neighborhood tavern whose burger keeps topping Madison lists — Isthmus' survey of burger heroes, Doug Moe's Madison Magazine column (Chicago magazine called it the top of 'burger heaven'), and UpNorthNews readers' best bar food 2025. Order: Char-grilled Oakcrest burger from Knoche's steak trimmings, ground daily.

    5371 Old Middleton Rd, Madison, WI 53705

    Recommended by Isthmus, Madison Magazine / Channel 3000, Upnorthnews

    1033 S Park St, Madison, WI 53715

    Recommended by Isthmus, The Cap Times, The Daily Cardinal (UW–Madison)

    Madison's long-running Thai standard-bearer — an Isthmus readers' Mad Faves Thai pick and a perennial Madison Magazine Best of Madison winner. Order: Fish-sauce-free curries and noodles, voted Best of Madison since 1997.

    2840 University Ave, Madison, WI 53705

    Recommended by Isthmus, Destination Madison (CVB), Travel Wisconsin (WI Dept. of Tourism)

  16. Worth the detour · Friday Fish Fry · West side

    Sardine chefs Phillip Hurley and John Gadau's Monroe Street fish house–meets–Wisconsin tavern (opened 2012; Wisconsin State Journal); one of Travel Wisconsin's 8 Madison fish-fry picks; a Cap Times family-dining favourite.     3502 Monroe St, Madison, WI 53711

    Recommended by Travel Wisconsin (WI Dept. of Tourism), Wisconsin State Journal (madison.com), The Cap Times

    Recommended by Destination Madison (CVB), Wikipedia (notability + published coordinates)

  19. Worth the detour · Bakeries & Kringle · West side

    Kosher donut bakery since 1996 — gold for Bakery–Sweets in Best of Madison 2025 and 2026, UpNorthNews readers' best bakery in southern Wisconsin, #26 on a 2025 national best-donut-shops list. Order: Old-fashioned and apple-fritter donuts (Madison's only certified-kosher bakery).

    Greenbush neighborhood, Madison, WI

    Recommended by Madison Magazine / Channel 3000, Upnorthnews

    Recommended by Madison Magazine / Channel 3000, City Cast Madison

Order: Award-winning fish fry — cod and perch beer-battered with New Glarus Spotted Cow (Wednesdays & Fridays).

    Recommended by Madison Magazine / Channel 3000, Brava Magazine, Visit Middleton (Middleton Tourism Commission)

  11. Worth the detour · Middleton, Verona & Fitchburg

    7440 W Old Sauk Rd, Middleton (Town), WI 53562

    3050 Cahill Main #3, Fitchburg, WI 53711

    Recommended by Isthmus, The Cap Times

  17. Deep cut · Breweries, Wineries & Distilleries · Middleton, Verona & Fitchburg

    Hop Haus Brewing Co. (Verona)

    German-tavern brewpub on Verona's Main Street beside the Military Ridge State Trail (Isthmus, Verona Press); grew into a second Fitchburg brewery. Order: German-style lagers on the Military Ridge Trail.

    231 S Main St, Verona, WI 53593

    Recommended by Isthmus, Verona Press

Dane County towns 14

Mount Horeb, Stoughton, Sun Prairie, McFarland, Cross Plains, Mazomanie

  1. Must see · Dane County towns

    Cave of the Mounds

    A limestone show cave in the south slope of the East Blue Mound, discovered by quarrymen in 1939 — a National Natural Landmark (1987) that the Chicago Academy of Sciences called 'the significant cave of the upper Midwest'.

    Blue Mounds, WI 53517

    Recommended by NPS, Wikipedia (notability + published coordinates), showcaves.com

  2. Must see · Dane County towns

    Stoughton Opera House

    Stoughton's 1901 city-hall opera house, left to decay after 1953 and reopened in 2001 after a 20-year community restoration; 80+ shows a year in the Norwegian-heritage town. Celebrated 125 years in 2026.

    381 E Main St, Stoughton, WI 53589

    Recommended by Wikipedia (notability + published coordinates), WMTV 15 News, Brava Magazine

  3. Must see · Supper Clubs & Brandy Old Fashioneds · Dane County towns

    Dorf Haus Supper Club

    A Roxbury tavern-and-dance-hall turned German supper club, run by the Maier family since 1959. Gold for Fish Fry in Madison Magazine's Best of Madison 2025 and winner of its 'Most Fabulous Fish Fry' contest; Milwaukee Record calls it the Friday-night pilgrimage. Order: All-you-can-eat Friday haddock fish fry with potato pancakes/fritters, or jäger schnitzel with spaetzle.

    County Hwy Y, Roxbury (3 mi SE of Sauk City), WI

    Recommended by Madison Magazine / Channel 3000, Milwaukee Record, Travel Wisconsin (WI Dept. of Tourism)

  4. Must see · Breweries, Wineries & Distilleries · Dane County towns

    Grumpy Troll Brew Pub

    Brewpub in a 1916 creamery in the middle of the Trollway, open since 1998 and 'still packed every night' (Milwaukee Magazine's Mount Horeb–New Glarus day trip). Order: House ales and lagers and a Friday fish fry among the trolls.

    105 S Second St, Mount Horeb, WI 53572

    Recommended by Milwaukee Magazine, Travel Wisconsin (WI Dept. of Tourism), Midwest Weekends

  5. Must see · Breweries, Wineries & Distilleries · Dane County towns

    Wollersheim Winery

    Wisconsin's historic winery: Hungarian count Agoston Haraszthy planted these slopes in the 1840s before leaving to found California's wine industry; Peter Kehl's stone buildings are on the National Register. Now a winery, distillery and restaurant. Order: Estate wines and Wollersheim's own brandy, tasted in the 1840s-rooted stone cellars.

    Across the Wisconsin River east of Prairie du Sac, Dane County, WI

    Recommended by Wikipedia (notability + published coordinates), OnMilwaukee

  6. Worth the detour · Breweries, Wineries & Distilleries · Dane County towns

    Drumlin Ridge Winery

    Family winery (2017) on a glacial drumlin north of Madison with a 6,400 sq ft tasting room and patio; Best of Madison 2026 silver Wine Bar and bronze Winery; on Brava's Madison-area winery trail. Order: Estate wine or hard cider on the drumlin-top patio with a cheese board.

    Waunakee countryside (between Waunakee and Westport), WI

    Recommended by Madison Magazine / Channel 3000, Brava Magazine, Isthmus, Travel Wisconsin (WI Dept. of Tourism)

  7. Worth the detour · Dane County towns

    Blue Mound State Park

    The highest point in southern Wisconsin: two observation towers atop the West Blue Mound look north to the Baraboo Range and east to Madison, with mountain-bike and hiking trails and a hilltop pool.

    Blue Mounds, WI 53517 (Iowa & Dane counties)

    Recommended by Wikipedia (notability + published coordinates), Wisconsin DNR — State Parks, Travel Wisconsin (WI Dept. of Tourism)

  8. Worth the detour · Dane County towns

    Governor Nelson State Park

    A 422-acre day-use park on Lake Mendota's north shore with a sand beach, restored prairie and oak savanna — and an unusually large panther effigy mound on the Woodland Trail.

    North shore of Lake Mendota, Town of Westport (near Waunakee), WI

    Recommended by Wikipedia (notability + published coordinates), Travel Wisconsin (WI Dept. of Tourism), Destination Madison (CVB)

  9. Worth the detour · Supper Clubs & Brandy Old Fashioneds · Dane County towns

    Maple Tree Supper Club

    McFarland supper club serving the full supper-club ritual for 40+ years (City Cast); gold for Salad Bar in Best of Madison 2026. Order: Full salad bar and prime-rib specials.

    McFarland, WI

    Recommended by City Cast Madison, Madison Magazine / Channel 3000, Travel Wisconsin (WI Dept. of Tourism)

  10. Worth the detour · Breakfast, Cafés & Coffee · Dane County towns

    Firefly Coffeehouse

    'Oregon's living room' since 2000, in a former grocery; now run by Wisconsin Cheese Originals founder Jeanne Carpenter with an artisan cheese counter. Silver for Coffee Shop in Best of Madison 2025 and 2026. Order: Espresso and from-scratch bakery, plus a Wisconsin artisan-cheese case.

    Oregon, WI 53575

    Recommended by Madison Magazine / Channel 3000, Wkow 27 (Madison Abc), Isthmus

  11. Worth the detour · Breweries, Wineries & Distilleries · Dane County towns

    Brix Cider

    Mount Horeb cidery-restaurant pressing only locally grown apples, two-thirds of its kitchen sourced from Wisconsin farms (Isthmus, Brava); Travel Wisconsin-listed. Order: Small-batch cider from 18 area orchards, with house-made sausages.

    119 S 2nd St, Mount Horeb, WI 53572

    Recommended by Isthmus, Brava Magazine, Travel Wisconsin (WI Dept. of Tourism)

  12. Worth the detour · American & New American · Dane County towns

    Buck & Honey's

    Sun Prairie's big supper-house-style restaurant, a four-time Best of Madison gold winner in 2025 (best restaurant, bartender, outdoor dining, catering). Order: Steaks and an all-day American menu, with live music.

    804 Liberty Blvd, Sun Prairie, WI 53590

    Recommended by Madison Magazine / Channel 3000, Travel Wisconsin (WI Dept. of Tourism)

  13. Worth the detour · Supper Clubs & Brandy Old Fashioneds · Dane County towns

    Rex's Innkeeper

    Waunakee supper club popular for special-occasion banquets (City Cast's supper-club guide); silver for Salad Bar in Best of Madison 2026. Order: Supper-club salad bar and prime rib.

    Waunakee, WI

    Recommended by City Cast Madison, Madison Magazine / Channel 3000

  14. Deep cut · Dane County towns

    Lake Kegonsa State Park

    A 343-acre lakeside state park on Kegonsa's northeast shore, a few minutes from Norwegian-heritage Stoughton — beach, campground and prairie trails.

    2405 Door Creek Rd, Stoughton, WI 53589

    Recommended by Wikipedia (notability + published coordinates), Travel Wisconsin (WI Dept. of Tourism)

Day trips 24

Spring Green & Taliesin, New Glarus, House on the Rock, Devil's Lake & Baraboo

  1. Must see · Day trips

    Taliesin

    Frank Lloyd Wright's home, studio and 600-acre estate in the Wyoming Valley, the exemplar of the Prairie School — a UNESCO World Heritage Site since 2019 (the 20th-Century Architecture of Frank Lloyd Wright). Tours from the visitor center.

    5607 County Rd C, Spring Green, WI 53588

    Recommended by UNESCO World Heritage Centre, Wikipedia (notability + published coordinates), Frank Lloyd Wright Foundation

  2. Must see · Day trips

    House on the Rock

    Alex Jordan Jr.'s maximalist fever-dream (1945–59) atop a rock chimney near Spring Green — the cantilevered Infinity Room, automaton music machines and the world's largest indoor carousel. Time Out calls it a must from Madison; it sits minutes from Taliesin.

    5754 State Rd 23, Spring Green, WI 53588

    Recommended by Wikipedia (notability + published coordinates), Time Out — Madison, Travel Wisconsin (WI Dept. of Tourism)

  3. Must see · Day trips

    Devil's Lake State Park

    Wisconsin's largest state park (1911), a glacial lake ringed by 500-foot pink-quartzite bluffs in the Baraboo Range, 35 miles from Madison — the Devil's Doorway trail is the classic short climb.

    Devil's Lake State Park, south of Baraboo, Sauk County, WI

    Recommended by Wikipedia (notability + published coordinates), Upnorthnews, Wisconsin Historical Society

  4. Must see · Day trips

    International Crane Foundation

    The world's only collection of all 15 crane species, at the Baraboo headquarters of the conservation group founded by two Cornell ornithology students in 1973 — Tone Madison calls it the nature scene's must-see.

    E11376 Shady Lane Rd, Baraboo, WI 53913

    Recommended by Wikipedia (notability + published coordinates), Tone Madison, Experience Wisconsin magazine

  5. Must see · Day trips

    American Players Theatre

    Classical repertory theatre on 110 Driftless acres across the river from Spring Green: the 1,075-seat outdoor Hill Theatre in an oak-wooded hollow plus the indoor Touchstone. Nearly 100,000 visitors a season (June–November); 2026 Regional Theatre Tony Award.

    Spring Green (Iowa County side of the Wisconsin River), WI

    Recommended by American Theatre magazine, Telegraph Herald (Dubuque), Wikipedia (notability + published coordinates)

  6. Must see · Day trips

    Al. Ringling Theatre

    'America's Prettiest Playhouse' — a 1915 Rapp & Rapp movie palace commissioned by circus co-founder Al Ringling; shows, classic films, Barton organ demos and daily 1:30pm tours.

    136 4th Ave, Baraboo, WI

    Recommended by Wikipedia (notability + published coordinates), Travel Wisconsin (WI Dept. of Tourism), Wisconsin Historical Society

  7. Must see · Supper Clubs & Brandy Old Fashioneds · Day trips

    Ishnala Supper Club

    Summer-season supper club built in 1953 over Mirror Lake, with Norway pines growing through the floor; won in Best of Madison 2025 and profiled by Cook's Country as the archetype of the Wisconsin supper club. Order: A brandy old fashioned (sweet, sour or press) — 108,504 poured in 2023 — then prime rib over Mirror Lake.

    Mirror Lake (inside Mirror Lake State Park), Lake Delton, WI

    Recommended by Madison Magazine / Channel 3000, Cook's Country (America's Test Kitchen), Heavy Table

  8. Must see · Breweries, Wineries & Distilleries · Day trips

    New Glarus Brewing Co.

    The Swiss village's craft brewery, maker of Spotted Cow (Best of Madison 2026 gold for local craft beer, gold Brewery 2025 & 2026); Time Out names it the side-trip from Madison, and its Bavarian-style hilltop brewery has a self-guided tour and beer garden. Order: Spotted Cow — sold only in Wisconsin — in the hilltop beer garden.

    Hilltop brewery, New Glarus, WI 53574

    Recommended by Madison Magazine / Channel 3000, Time Out — Madison, Upnorthnews

  9. Must see · Breweries, Wineries & Distilleries · Day trips

    Driftless Glen Distillery

    Baraboo craft distillery with a riverfront restaurant whose menu is cooked with its own spirits; Best of Madison 2026 gold for Outdoor Dining and bronze for Old Fashioned and Bloody Mary, plus a 2025 Bar medal. Order: A Driftless Glen brandy old fashioned on the Baraboo River patio; brandy-glazed salmon.

    Baraboo River, Baraboo, WI

    Recommended by Madison Magazine / Channel 3000, The Cap Times, Travel Wisconsin (WI Dept. of Tourism)

  10. Must see · Supper Clubs & Brandy Old Fashioneds · Day trips

    The Del-Bar

    Supper club run by the Wimmer family since 1943, its stone-and-glass building designed by Taliesin-trained James Dresser in Wright's organic style; celebrated 80 years in 2023. Best of Madison 2026 silver for Destination Restaurant and Steakhouse, bronze for Supper Club. Order: Prime rib or a steak and a relish tray under Wright-protégé architecture.

    Lake Delton, WI

    Recommended by Madison Magazine / Channel 3000, WMTV 15 News, Wisconsin Historical Society

  11. Must see · Cheese Curds & Cheese · Day trips

    Baumgartner's Cheese Store & Tavern

    Wisconsin's oldest cheese store (1931) in Monroe, the Green County seat where the nation's last Limburger plant still runs; a Saveur 100 pick for its Limburger sandwich, also featured by Tasting Table. Order: The Limburger sandwich — three slices on rye with raw onion and mustard — and a local bock.

    Monroe, WI 53566

    Recommended by Saveur (Saveur 100), Tasting Table, WMTV 15 News

  12. Worth the detour · Day trips

    Circus World Museum

    The Ringling Brothers' winter quarters (1884–1918), now a Wisconsin Historical Society museum of circus wagons and history with summer big-top shows — a National Historic Landmark.

    550 Water St, Baraboo, WI 53913

    Recommended by NPS, Wikipedia (notability + published coordinates), Wisconsin Historical Society

  13. Worth the detour · Day trips

    Pendarvis

    Restored 1840s stone and log cottages of Cornish lead miners on Mineral Point's Shake Rag Street, run as a Wisconsin Historical Society site — pair it with a Cornish pasty in town.

    114 Shake Rag St, Mineral Point, WI 53565

    Recommended by Wisconsin Historical Society, Wikipedia (notability + published coordinates), Saharchipedia

  14. Worth the detour · Day trips

    Aldo Leopold Shack and Farm

    The worn-out farm and converted chicken coop where Aldo Leopold's family replanted pines and prairie in the 1930s — the place that grew 'A Sand County Almanac'. A National Historic Landmark (2009); tours via the Aldo Leopold Foundation.

    South bank of the Wisconsin River, northeast of Baraboo, WI

    Recommended by NPS, Wikipedia (notability + published coordinates), Wisconsin Public Radio

  15. Worth the detour · Day trips

    Chalet of the Golden Fleece

    A 1937–38 Bernese mountain chalet (NRHP) built for Wilhelm Tell pageant founder Edwin Barlow and given to the village as a museum in 1955 — Swiss folk art plus oddities like a Louis XVI watch and Etruscan earrings. Open Saturdays late May–October and festival weekends.

    618 2nd St, New Glarus, WI 53574

    Recommended by Wikipedia (notability + published coordinates), Travel Wisconsin (WI Dept. of Tourism), Wisconsin Historical Society

  16. Worth the detour · Day trips

    Seth Peterson Cottage

    One of Wright's last designs, a tiny stone-and-glass cottage over Mirror Lake — the first Wright house anywhere you can rent overnight; open-house tours monthly.

    E9982 Fern Dell Rd (Mirror Lake State Park), Reedsburg, WI

    Recommended by Wikipedia (notability + published coordinates), Frank Lloyd Wright Foundation, Wisconsin DNR — State Parks

  17. Worth the detour · Day trips

    Tower Hill State Park

    Small state park on the Wisconsin River bluff with the reconstructed Helena Shot Tower (1832) and its 120-foot shaft through the sandstone; NRHP.

    SE of Spring Green, Iowa County, WI

    Recommended by Wikipedia (notability + published coordinates), Wisconsin DNR — State Parks, Wisconsin Historical Society

  18. Worth the detour · Day trips

    Mid-Continent Railway Museum

    Golden-age steam railroading west of Baraboo — a 7-mile round trip on C&NW track behind historic locomotives (NRHP-listed C&NW 1385).

    E8948 Museum Rd, North Freedom, WI 53951

    Recommended by Trains magazine (Trains.com), The Clio, Wikipedia (notability + published coordinates)

  19. Worth the detour · Breweries, Wineries & Distilleries · Day trips

    Bailey's Run Vineyard

    Hilltop New Glarus winery (2018) with ~30 wines, Green County small plates and weekend live music; Best of Madison winery medals 2023–2026; profiled by Brava and Northwest Quarterly. Order: A flight of estate wines with a brick-oven Neapolitan pizza on weekends.

    New Glarus, WI 53574

    Recommended by Madison Magazine / Channel 3000, Brava Magazine, Northwest Quarterly

  20. Worth the detour · Breweries, Wineries & Distilleries · Day trips

    Minhas Craft Brewery

    The Midwest's oldest brewery (1845, ex-Joseph Huber) and the second-oldest in the U.S. (Wikipedia, Tasting Table); State Trunk Tour attraction pick. Order: A tour of the 1845 brewery and its brewery-memorabilia museum.

    1208 14th Ave, Monroe, WI 53566

    Recommended by Wikipedia (notability + published coordinates), State Trunk Tour, Tasting Table

  21. Worth the detour · Day trips

    Natural Bridge State Park

    Wisconsin's largest natural sandstone arch, with the Raddatz rock shelter beneath it — one of the oldest dated human occupation sites in the upper Midwest.

    Town of Honey Creek, southwest of Baraboo, Sauk County, WI

    Recommended by Wikipedia (notability + published coordinates), Wisconsin DNR — State Parks

  22. Worth the detour · Day trips

    Wyoming Valley School

    Wright's 1956 two-room schoolhouse built in honor of his kindergarten-teacher mother, now a cultural arts center a few miles from Taliesin; a stop on Wisconsin's 200-mile Frank Lloyd Wright Trail.

    6306 WI Hwy 23, Wyoming (Iowa County), WI

    Recommended by Wikipedia (notability + published coordinates), Chicago Sun-Times

  23. Worth the detour · Day trips

    A. D. German Warehouse

    Wright's 1921 Mayan Revival brick-and-concrete warehouse in his birthplace town — the western-most stop on the Frank Lloyd Wright Trail.

    316 S Church St, Richland Center, WI

    Recommended by Wikipedia (notability + published coordinates), Chicago Sun-Times

  24. Worth the detour · American & New American · Day trips

    Suzy's Pointer Cafe

    Mineral Point family diner on State Trunk Tour's 2026 guide to Wisconsin pasty shops — the Cornish miners' pasty in the town they settled. Order: A Cornish pasty with homemade pie.

    809 Ridge St, Mineral Point, WI 53565

    Recommended by State Trunk Tour, Travel Wisconsin (WI Dept. of Tourism)

66 sights and 90 places to eat across Madison — the Capitol Square isthmus, the UW campus, the east and west sides — plus Middleton, Verona, the Dane County towns and the classic day trips (Taliesin, New Glarus, Devil’s Lake), each traceable to the source that named it. The canon is Wisconsin’s own: squeaky cheese curds, the Friday fish fry, supper clubs and the brandy old fashioned, the Dane County Farmers’ Market, Babcock Hall ice cream, Hmong & Lao kitchens and New Glarus beer.

How this guide was made

How the cuisine filters were policed

Every food card names a specific dish — a cuisine label alone doesn’t qualify. Madison’s canon is Wisconsin’s own: fresh and fried cheese curds, the Friday fish fry, supper clubs and the brandy old fashioned sweet, the producer-only Dane County Farmers’ Market on the Capitol Square, Babcock Hall ice cream, brats and butter burgers, the city’s Hmong and Lao kitchens, and New Glarus beer. Kringle is a Racine tradition — where Madison has no standout, the gap is stated rather than filled. A cuisine tag names the kitchen’s own tradition, never one dish it happens to serve.

Web-searched and fact-checked

Every place is traceable to at least two credible sources (or one institutional authority such as the James Beard Foundation or the National Park Service) — the Wisconsin State Journal, The Cap Times, Isthmus, Madison Magazine, WPR, Travel Wisconsin, Destination Madison and vetted creators — recorded in data/sources.json. Every coordinate is verified into data/geocodes.json and every place status-checked. Yelp/TripAdvisor never count toward the two-source bar.
